title: Transductive Generalization for GNNs via Optimal Transport
claim: Feature-geometry measures (intra-class concentration and inter-class separation) track the generalization gap non-monotonically as depth grows, across models and datasets.
layout: 2x4 grid of line plots, paired Wasserstein/error panels, shared depth axis
description: A 2x4 grid of line charts. Rows are Cora (top) and CiteSeer (bottom). Columns come in pairs: (a) SGC Wasserstein, (b) SGC generalization error, (c) GCN Wasserstein, (d) GCN generalization error. The x-axis is network depth, from 1 to 32. The Wasserstein panels show a red square line (W_C) and a blue triangle line (W_S). The generalization error panels show a green diamond line with a light green shaded band for ±1 standard deviation. For SGC, the Wasserstein curves fall smoothly while generalization error rises slightly and then declines. For GCN, the curves rise to a peak around depth 8, drop sharply near depth 20-24, then partly recover, and the error curve follows the same pattern. Y-axes on the GCN Wasserstein panels are log-scaled. Legends sit in the top-right corner of each panel. Captions (a)-(d) run along the bottom.
caption: Depth analysis on Cora (top row) and CiteSeer (bottom row) for SGC and GCN, showing Wasserstein distances $\gW_C, \gW_S$ and the empirical generalization error denoted Gen. error in the figure at varying depths. Shaded regions indicate $\pm 1$ standard deviation across runs.
abstract: Analyzing the generalization of graph neural networks (GNNs) on node classification is challenging: message passing induces dependencies that break the i.i.d. assumption underlying standard inductive generalization theory. While distribution-free transductive theory resolves this dependency issue, existing classical bounds are either intractable or correlate poorly with empirical generalization. To fill this gap, we propose a transductive generalization bound based on optimal transport, connecting generalization to intra-class concentration and inter-class separation in the feature space. Empirically, our bound aligns strongly with the generalization gap. Building on this representation-based approach, we analyze how feature geometry evolves under repeated message passing. This explains the non-monotonic relationship between GNN depth and generalization, providing new insights into oversmoothing research. Practically, our bound serves as a geometry-aware regularizer that corrects the harmful behavior of message passing, yielding consistent performance improvements. The code is available at https://github.com/ml-postech/Transductive-OT-Gen-Bound.
